questions.knowledge_point: Finding Two Linearly Independent Complex Eigenvectors of a 2x2 Matrix
questions.problem:
Given that ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {b}_{1}\end{aligned}]$ and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{2} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ are linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 10 \\ -5 & 12\end{aligned}],$
what is the value of $\frac{{a}_{1}{a}_{2}}{{b}_{1}{b}_{2}}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the eigenvalues of $A.$ To do that, we must solve the characteristic equation $det(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 10 \\ -5 & 12-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-2-\lambda )(12-\lambda )-(-5)(10) & =0 \\ -24+2\lambda -12\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+50 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-10\lambda +26 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{-b\pm \sqrt{{b}^{2}-4ac}}{2a} \\  & =\frac{10\pm \sqrt{(-10)^{2}-4(1)(26)}}{2} \\  & =\frac{10\pm \sqrt{-4}}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{10\pm 2\text{i}}{2} \\  & =5\pm \text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =5\pm \text{i}.$

Now, let's consider the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}=5-\text{i}.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-{\lambda }_{1}I & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 10 \\ -5 & 12\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}5-\text{i} & 0 \\ 0 & 5-\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-7+\text{i} & 10 \\ -5 & 7+\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we get the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}(-7+\text{i}){x}_{1}+10{x}_{2}=0 \\ -5{x}_{1}+(7+\text{i}){x}_{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since the matrix $A-(5-2\text{i})I$ is singular, the system above must have a non-zero solution. This means that one equation of the system is a multiple of another. As a result, we can drop one of the rows and take one of the variables as the free variable. For example, from the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{1}{5}(7+\text{i}){x}_{2}
$$

Hence, the general solution is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{5}(7+\text{i}){x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in C.
$$

Setting ${x}_{2}=5,$ we get the eigenvector

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}7+\text{i} \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Then, to compute the second eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=5+\text{i}$, we simply compute the complex conjugate of ${\overset{―}{v}}_{1},$ and get

$$
{v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}7-\text{i} \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{a}_{1}{a}_{2}}{{b}_{1}{b}_{2}} & =\frac{(7+\text{i})(7-\text{i})}{(5)(5)}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
If $v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 \\ 13 & 1\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-1+3\text{i},$
then what is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =-1+3\text{i},$ and

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 \\ 13 & 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1+3\text{i} & 0 \\ 0 & -1+3\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2-3\text{i} & -1 \\ 13 & 2-3\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}(-2-3\text{i}){x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0 \\ 13{x}_{1}+(2-3\text{i}){x}_{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since the matrix $A-(-1+3\text{i})I$ is singular, the system above must have a non-zero solution. This means that one equation of the system is a multiple of another. As a result, we can drop one of the rows and take one of the variables to be the free variable. For example, from the first equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}=(-2-3\text{i}){x}_{1}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ -(2+3\text{i}){x}_{1}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{1}\in C.
$$

Setting ${x}_{1}=-1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2+3\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{-1}{2+3\text{i}}=\frac{-(2-3\text{i})}{13}=-\frac{2}{13}+\frac{3}{13}\text{i}.$

questions.problem:
If $v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ -3 & -2\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =\sqrt{5}\text{i},$
then what is the value of $\frac{b}{a}?$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =\sqrt{5}\text{i},$ and

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ -3 & -2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{5}\text{i} & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt{5}\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2-\sqrt{5}\text{i} & 3 \\ -3 & -2-\sqrt{5}\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}(2-\sqrt{5}\text{i}){x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0 \\ -3{x}_{1}+(-2-\sqrt{5}\text{i}){x}_{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since the matrix $A-\sqrt{5}\text{i}I$ is singular, the system above must have a non-zero solution. This means that one equation of the system is a multiple of another. As a result, we can drop one of the rows and take one of the variables to be the free variable. For example, from the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{3}(2+\sqrt{5}\text{i}){x}_{2}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3}(2+\sqrt{5}\text{i}){x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in C.
$$

Setting ${x}_{2}=-3,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}2+\sqrt{5}\text{i} \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $\frac{b}{a}=\frac{-3}{2+\sqrt{5}\text{i}}=\frac{-3(2-\sqrt{5}\text{i})}{9}=-\frac{2}{3}+\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\text{i}.$

questions.problem:
If $v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 10 \\ -2 & 7\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =5-4\text{i},$
then what is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
questions.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =5-4\text{i},$ and

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 10 \\ -2 & 7\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}5-4\text{i} & 0 \\ 0 & 5-4\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2+4\text{i} & 10 \\ -2 & 2+4\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}(-2+4\text{i}){x}_{1}+10{x}_{2}=0 \\ -2{x}_{1}+(2+4\text{i}){x}_{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since the matrix $A-(5-4\text{i})I$ is singular, the system above must have a non-zero solution. This means that one equation of the system is a multiple of another. As a result, we can drop one of the rows and take one of the variables to be the free variable. For example, from the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{1}=(1+2\text{i}){x}_{2}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}(1+2\text{i}){x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in C.
$$

Setting ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1+2\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{1+2\text{i}}{1}=1+2\text{i}.$

questions.problem:
Given that ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {b}_{1}\end{aligned}]$ and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{2} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ are linearly independent eigenvectors of the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 \\ -5 & 3\end{aligned}],$
what is the value of $\frac{{b}_{1}{b}_{2}}{{a}_{1}{a}_{2}}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the eigenvalues of $A.$ To do that, we must solve the characteristic equation $det(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}7-\lambda  & 4 \\ -5 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (7-\lambda )(3-\lambda )-(4)(-5) & =0 \\ 21-7\lambda -3\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}+20 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-10\lambda +41 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda  & =\frac{-b\pm \sqrt{{b}^{2}-4ac}}{2a} \\  & =\frac{-(-10)\pm \sqrt{(-10)^{2}-4(1)(41)}}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{-(-10)\pm \sqrt{-64}}{2} \\  & =\frac{10\pm 8\text{i}}{2} \\  & =5\pm 4\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda =5\pm 4\text{i}.$

Now, let's consider the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}=5+4\text{i}.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-{\lambda }_{1}I & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 \\ -5 & 3\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}5+4\text{i} & 0 \\ 0 & 5+4\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2-4\text{i} & 4 \\ -5 & -2-4\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we get the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}(2-4\text{i}){x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=0 \\ -5{x}_{1}+(-2-4\text{i}){x}_{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since the matrix $A-(5+4\text{i})I$ is singular, the system above must have a non-zero solution. This means that one equation of the system is a multiple of another. As a result, we can drop one of the rows and take one of the variables as the free variable. For example, from the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{1}{5}(-2-4\text{i}){x}_{2}
$$

Hence, the general solution is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{5}(-2-4\text{i}){x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in C.
$$

Setting ${x}_{2}=-5,$ we get the eigenvector

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2+4\text{i} \\ -5\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Then, to compute the second eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=5-4\text{i}$, we simply compute the complex conjugate of ${\overset{―}{v}}_{1},$ and get

$$
{v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2-4\text{i} \\ -5\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{b}_{1}{b}_{2}}{{a}_{1}{a}_{2}} & =\frac{(-5)(-5)}{(2+4\text{i})(2-4\text{i})}=\frac{5}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
